subject: Order Form Exhibit: surge protection, packaging transition and redline questions
messages:
From: Amelia Carter <amelia.carter@helioshealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Marcus Reed <marcus.reed@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on Exhibit B — surge protection + packaging transition

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of items on Exhibit B that our procurement and cloud finance teams asked me to get clarified before legal signs off:

1) Surge protection trigger — the current language references a "temporary surcharge" when burst > 150% of committed throughput. Our finance folks want to cap the per-token surcharge during a surge window (e.g., not more than 2x list rate) and also have a defined lookback window to calculate sustained surges.

2) Packaging / tier transition — if usage crosses into a higher bucket mid-quarter, we need clarity on how the pro-rata conversion is handled and whether any retroactive true-up applies for the days prior to the transition.

3) Fallback behavior — we need a short fallback SLA if the dedicated model variant isn't available: is automatic routing to a compatible model variant acceptable, and how would that affect billing?

Attached is our annotated Exhibit B (Helios_ExhibitB_marked.pdf) and a simple billing calc from our side (provisional-billing-sheet.xlsx) so you can see the scenarios that worry us.

Can your team propose redline language for the surcharge cap + lookback window and confirm billing treatment for fallback/routing? We are aiming to close by the end of next week.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Carter
Sr. Procurement Manager, Helios Health

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Carter <amelia.carter@helioshealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-19T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B — surge protection + packaging transition

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Looping in Ben (AE) and Jordan (Contracts) to draft precise redlines. High-level answers first:

- Surge surcharge cap: we can accept an explicit cap during a burst window; typical market practice we use is up to 1.8x list for transient surges but we are open to 2x where justified.
- Lookback / smoothing: we can define a 7-day rolling lookback to determine sustained surges and limit churning.
- Packaging transition: our platform supports pro-rata transitions; true-ups are typically applied at month-end on a net basis.
- Fallback routing: automatic routing to a compatible model variant is supported. Billing differs depending on variant (we bill by token unit of the served model). We can include a clause that preserves customer notice and a credit mechanism if fallback materially degrades QoE.

Ben/Jordan — can you take Amelia's markup and draft redline language for the three items above? Jordan, please include an ops-friendly definition for "sustained surge" (we proposed 7-day rolling) and a short fallback credit formula.

Tessa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Carter <amelia.carter@helioshealth.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-20T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B — surge protection + packaging transition

Amelia — attaching an initial draft redline (redline-orderform.docx) for Exhibit B and a short example calc embedded below. Laura from Legal is cc'ed for final language.

Draft summary (high level):
- Surge surcharge: "During any Surge Window (defined below), Customer shall not be charged more than 1.95x Redwood's then-current published list rate per token for the specific model variant actually served. For the avoidance of doubt, any surcharge applied under this Section shall not exceed 1.95x list rate."

- Surge Window definition: "Surge Window" means any continuous period where peak sustained throughput exceeds 150% of Customer's committed throughput as measured on a 24-hour rolling basis. A sustained surge for contract remediation (i.e., step or tier change) requires exceeding 150% for at least 7 consecutive days as measured on a rolling 7-day basis.

- Packaging transition / prorata: "If Customer's aggregated usage for a calendar month crosses into the next commitment band, Redwood will pro-rate the new band's pricing for the remaining days of the month. Any month-end true-up will reconcile billed amounts against committed bands and will reflect the pro-rated rates; no retroactive billing for prior days will exceed the pro-rated amounts."

- Fallback credit: "If Redwood routes requests to a materially lower-quality model variant for more than 4 consecutive hours and such routing is not requested or approved by Customer, Redwood will issue a service credit equal to 10% of the token charges invoiced during the impacted period. Material degradation will be determined by mutual measurement of response latency and model output pass-rate on a pre-agreed evaluation set."

Example (from your spreadsheet): if a 7-day surge would push you from Tier B to Tier C and the billing calc shows X, the surcharge cap limits per-token surcharge and the month-end true-up will reconcile across the band transition.

I'll wait for Laura and Jordan to add contract polish. Amelia — happy to hop on a 30m call to walk the language through.

— Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Carter <amelia.carter@helioshealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-21T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B — surge protection + packaging transition

Amelia — thanks for the patience. I reviewed Ben's draft and made two legal-focused edits in the attached redline: (1) clarified that the 1.95x cap is a cap on surcharge components and does not alter base list pricing mechanics; (2) tightened the fallback credit measurement to use a mutually agreed evaluation set that will be attached as a schedule after signature (to avoid post-signature disputes).

One point to flag for your finance team: the pro-rata language is forward-looking for the month of transition; we do not permit retro-billing beyond the current invoice cycle, but we will perform a reconciliation true-up at month-end that may result in a credit or an additional charge depending on net usage. Irene (cc) can confirm how credits would be applied in our billing system.

If Helios is comfortable with 1.95x and the 7-day sustained threshold, we can prepare an updated Exhibit B for signature with an attached Schedule A (evaluation set) to cover fallback measurement.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Reed <marcus.reed@helioshealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Amelia Carter <amelia.carter@helioshealth.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B — surge protection + packaging transition

Laura / Tessa / Team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed redline. Helios is generally comfortable with the 1.95x cap and the 7-day sustained definition, but would like the following small edits before we proceed to signature: (a) make the "Surge Window" measurement timezone-agnostic and anchor it to UTC; (b) add a clause that the fallback credit calculation will be trued up at the next invoice cycle rather than applied immediately as an off-cycle credit.

We will review Ben's example calc with internal finance and aim to return a final mark by EOD Friday. If you can send the redline with Laura's Schedule A placeholder and the UTC anchor, that will let Legal and Procurement move to DocuSign.

Marcus Reed
Head of Cloud Procurement, Helios Health
